daily_reality.summary: CV techs perform diagnostic cardiac and vascular tests including EKGs, echocardiograms, stress tests, and assist with cardiac catheterization. They work in hospitals, cath labs, and outpatient clinics. Typical 40-hour week with on-call requirements for cath lab staff.
typical_tasks: Attaching electrodes and operating EKG machines to record heart rhythms
Assisting cardiologists during cardiac catheterization procedures
Preparing patients: shaving, cleansing insertion sites, administering topical anesthesia
Monitoring patients' blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation during procedures
Operating and interpreting vascular ultrasound (duplex scanning)
Entering data into PACS and EHR systems
Transcribing and distributing diagnostic reports for physician interpretation

deadlines.stat_ekg: Immediate — results needed within minutes for emergencies
deadlines.equipment_calibration: Per manufacturer schedule and facility protocol
deadlines.ce_renewal: 30 CME units every 3 years (ARDMS) or 16-36 CEUs every 3 years (CCI)

daily_reality.seasonality: Heart-related emergencies have no strict seasonality but cardiac events increase in winter months. Elective procedures may slow during holiday periods. Cath lab on-call is year-round.

regulatory.summary: Certification through CCI or ARDMS is the industry standard though not legally required in most states. Only 5 states mandate licensure (NH, NM, ND, OR, WA). CAAHEP accredits training programs. Continuing education required for credential maintenance.

key_laws.name: State licensure laws (NH, NM, ND, OR, WA)
key_laws.description: Only 5 states currently mandate licensure for cardiovascular technologists

key_laws.name: CAAHEP accreditation standards
key_laws.description: Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs accredits CV tech training programs

key_laws.name: CMS Conditions of Participation
key_laws.description: Medicare/Medicaid standards requiring qualified staff for cardiac diagnostic services

requirements: Associate's or bachelor's degree in cardiovascular technology (CAAHEP-accredited preferred)

CCI credentials: RCIS (Registered Cardiovascular Invasive Specialist), RCS (Registered Cardiac Sonographer), RVS (Registered Vascular Specialist), RCES (Registered Cardiac Electrophysiology Specialist)
ARDMS credentials: RDCS (Registered Diagnostic Cardiac Sonographer), RVT (Registered Vascular Technologist)
Continuing education: 30 CME/3 years (ARDMS) or 16-36 CEU/3 years (CCI)
Annual ARDMS renewal fee by December 31

regulatory.recent_changes: Increasing employer requirements for certification even in states without licensure mandates. Growing push for standardized national certification requirements.

tools.summary: Specialized cardiology equipment including echocardiography machines, EKG systems, cardiac catheterization lab equipment, and vascular ultrasound. Software centers on Cardiology PACS and EHR integration using DICOM, HL7, and FHIR standards.

primary_tools.name: Echocardiography machines
primary_tools.description: Ultrasound systems for cardiac imaging — GE Vivid, Philips EPIQ, Siemens ACUSON

primary_tools.name: Cardiac catheterization lab equipment
primary_tools.description: Fluoroscopy systems, hemodynamic monitoring, IVUS, FFR measurement tools

primary_tools.name: Cardiology PACS
primary_tools.description: Picture archiving system for cardiac imaging — stores and distributes echo, cath, and CT images

primary_tools.name: EHR systems (cardiology modules)
primary_tools.description: Electronic health records with cardiology-specific templates and data integration

primary_tools.name: Vascular ultrasound systems
primary_tools.description: Duplex/color Doppler systems for arterial and venous assessment

secondary_tools: Holter monitors and event recorders for ambulatory monitoring
pain_points: Multiple non-integrated software systems (PACS, EHR, reporting)
Complex workflows for data transfer between systems
On-call demands with no dedicated workspace

terminology.summary: Highly technical medical vocabulary combining cardiology, ultrasound physics, and hemodynamics. Many abbreviations used in daily communication.

terms.EKG/ECG: Electrocardiogram — recording of heart's electrical activity
terms.TEE: Transesophageal echocardiogram — echo via esophagus probe
terms.EF: Ejection fraction — percentage of blood pumped per heartbeat (normal 55-70%)
terms.IVUS: Intravascular ultrasound — catheter-based imaging inside vessels
terms.FFR: Fractional flow reserve — measures pressure across coronary blockage
terms.STEMI: ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction — heart attack requiring emergency cath
terms.Doppler: Ultrasound technique measuring blood flow velocity and direction
terms.hemodynamics: Study of blood flow and pressure in the cardiovascular system
terms.sheath: Tube inserted into artery/vein for catheter access
terms.wall motion: Assessment of heart muscle movement patterns on echo
terms.regurgitation: Backward leaking of blood through a heart valve
terms.stenosis: Narrowing of a blood vessel or heart valve

career_psychology.summary: Hands-on healthcare career with moderate education (associate's degree). Strong job security due to aging population and cardiovascular disease prevalence. Median salary ~$62,000. Career advancement through specialization (invasive, echo, vascular) and additional credentials.
career_path: Associate's degree in cardiovascular technology (2 years, CAAHEP-accredited)
Entry-level EKG technician or non-invasive CV tech
Specialized technologist: echocardiography, invasive (cath lab), or vascular
Educator or applications specialist for equipment vendors
fears: Losing certification due to insufficient CE credits
Being replaced by AI-assisted automated readings
Physical strain from standing and patient positioning
motivation: Direct role in life-saving cardiac care
burnout_factors: Physical demands of patient positioning and long procedures
High patient volume with tight schedules

associations.type: Credentialing body for cardiac and vascular sonographers

market.summary: Growing demand driven by aging population and cardiovascular disease prevalence. BLS projects 7% growth 2023-2033. Cardiovascular disease remains #1 cause of death in the US, sustaining demand for diagnostic services.
market_trends: Aging baby boomer population increasing cardiovascular diagnostic volume
Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) expanding into more settings
AI-assisted echo interpretation emerging but not replacing techs
Hybrid cardiovascular procedures requiring cross-trained technologists
Growing demand in outpatient and ambulatory settings
